earlier.claim: The out-of-band `nomad job stop ov-dash` is recorded only in .okf/nodes/orangepi4a.md (Quirks) and .okf/components/seaweedfs.md. Both say minio-removal starts ov-dash again, but .loop/plans/minio-removal.md has no such step and never names ov-dash. .okf/components/ov-dash.md does not say the job is stopped, and the orangepi4a jobs table still lists ov-dash as running there. The applications-root tickets in this epic (seaweedfs-buckets, seaweedfs-workload-identity, the cutovers) will see nomad_job.ov_dash as drift in `terraform plan`, and an apply re-registers it to queue for memory beside SeaweedFS, with nothing telling them why. As it stands, ov-dash can stay down for good once MinIO is gone.

test_master_grows_two_volumes_per_collection checks only that the text `[master.volume_growth] copy_1 = 2` appears in the jobspec. It does not check that the file is mounted at /etc/seaweedfs/master.toml, so if the `volumes` mount is dropped or the path changes, the test still passes while the growth setting is gone, which r1's fails_when covers. The live six-bucket check cannot catch this either, because `-volume.max=0` on a TiB volume gives plenty of slots under the default copy_1 = 7.

The .okf/summary.md 'Where it stands' section still says SeaweedFS 'is planned to replace' MinIO. It now runs beside MinIO on orangepi4a and has cost the cluster ov-dash. Update the line, or run `kmctl summary ack` if the operator judges it still right, per CLAUDE.md duty 5.

new.claim: minio-removal step 6 offers `nomad job eval ov-dash` as a way to start the stopped job, but evaluating a job with Stop=true places nothing; only a re-register (an applications-root apply or nomad job run) starts it
